correctness.rationale: Tree resistance decomposition gives an exact strictly convex separable reciprocal-weight objective. Explicit candidate satisfies stochastic constraints; the first junction is strictly slack by a universal nonnegative-coefficient identity, and all other KKT multipliers are nonnegative by exact symbolic polynomial identities for both parity cases, with final multiplier zero. Strict convexity and leaf automorphisms give unrestricted unique global optimum. Exact supplementary 216-case checks and direct eigenvalue traces agree; these are not substituted for the proof.

Direct published-finding corpus synonym/parameter/equivalence searches yielded close but distinct path, spider, minimax and spectral-gap results. The restricted all-size closed-form optimizer is not a corollary of the statements examined. Residual priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: No literature search establishes absolute novelty; an unindexed exact theorem may exist.
The full Kirkland–Zeng 2016 paper was inaccessible; only its public abstract/excerpt was compared.
The 2015 and 2026 general optimization works solve fixed-size instances algorithmically; their general framework is known and is not claimed novel.

value.rationale: An entire natural infinite branching-tree family has an unknown exact optimum for a motivated Kemeny minimization problem. The explicit active holding set has one genuinely free interior junction next to the hub while all later interior path vertices are saturated, a structural distinction from stochastic paths. Closed square-root weights, exact objective, and nontrivial first-edge scaling are potentially useful for network circulation design without a general downstream theorem.
